steps.title: Volcanic soils
steps.body: Etna's soils are made of volcanic sand, ash and lava, of different ages. They're poor, well-drained and rich in minerals. Each lava flow created different soils, so neighbouring vineyards can taste different. Phylloxera struggles in volcanic sand, so many old vines are ungrafted, trained as alberello, bush vines, on terraces.

steps.title: Contrade
steps.body: Etna's vineyards are divided into contrade, local districts, often defined by lava flows. In 2011, Etna DOC recognised 133 contrade, which can appear on labels, like Burgundy's crus. Producers like Frank Cornelissen, Andrea Franchetti of Passopisciaro and Marc de Grazia drove Etna's revival from the early 2000s.

steps.prompt: Why are many Etna vines ungrafted?
steps.explanation: Sandy volcanic soils protect against phylloxera, so many old vines survive on their own roots.

steps.body: Look for a contrada name on an Etna label, such as Rampante or Feudo di Mezzo. Like a Burgundy cru, it tells you exactly where the grapes grew.

steps.explanation: Contrade are local districts, often defined by lava flows.
